newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices stronger in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices stronger in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices moved steadily upwards at sales in Sydney, Geelong and Fremantle this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly market review.

The eastern market indicator rose 16 cents to 608 cents a kg clean while the western market indicator rose nine cents to 582 cents a kg clean. A total of 78,983 bales were offered, of which the trade bought 93.6 percent. The pass-in rate was 6.4 percent.

"Prices rebounded fairly strongly at sales this week, reversing the downward trend which had occured over the three previous weeks," the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in its weekly market report.

Wesfarmers said there was more widespread competition in the market this week which meant less reliance on Japanese trading houses and on orders from China, which had been the pattern of recent weeks. This led most buyers to conclude that current prices will at least be maintained with the prospect of further increases in prices if the volume of new business picks up, Wesfarmers said.
Wool International said its stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,863,270 bales as of Thursday.
In the futures market, a total of 182 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended Thursday.
